senses: to free feet from snares; unfasten fetters; lose the shackles
to loosen restraints, unchain, set free, liberate, release
to unwind, untangle, untie, unwrap; disconnect, detach, extricate from entanglements
to remove impediments, clear obstacles; hasten, expedite a process
to make ready; prepare, develop, produce
to carry out, make happen, effect; arrange, settle a matter
to carry forth, bring forward; send out, dispatch, expedite
to be profitable, serviceable, advantageous, expedient
la:verb:expedio.html:
ex-pĕdĭo, īvi or ĭi, ītum, 4 (archaic
fut. expedibo, Enn., Pac., Att., and Pompon. ap. ; ; ), v. a.
pes
, orig., to free the feet, i. e. from a snare; hence, in gen., to extricate, disengage, let loose, set free, liberate any thing entangled, involved (class.; esp. freq. in the trop. signif.; syn.: extrico, enodo, enucleo, explico, expono, interpretor, etc.).
Lit.: videte, in quot se laqueos induerit, quorum ex nullo se umquam expediet,; cf. , § 106: mortis laqueis caput,; cf. also: vix illigatum te triformi Pegasus expediet Chimaera,: flammam inter et hostes Expedior,make my way through,: errantem nemori, et saep.—With inanim. and abstr. objects: aditus expediunt,open a passage,: sibi locum,: iter fugae per invias rupes,: agrum saxosum lectione lapidum,: capillus pectine quotidie expediendus est, disentangled, Fronto de Eloqu. init.—
Transf.
In gen., to fetch out, bring forward, procure, make ready, prepare any thing folded up, put away, etc.: funes expediunt, Sisenn. ap. : vela,: hominem nudari et virgas expediri jubet,: cererem canistris,: convivia mediis tectis (famulae),; cf.: cibaria pastoribus,to provide,: merces suas (institor),: pecuniam, to procure, ap. ; : arma,to hold in readiness,; ; : tela equosque,: ferrum,: naves,: vineas in occulto,: copias,: se celeriter (Galli equites),: se,; ; cf. mid.: exercitum expediri ad bellum jubet,. —
to send away, despatch (poet.): me ex suis locis pulcre ornatum expedivit,: saepe disco, Saepe trans finem jaculo nobilis expedito, despatched, i. e. hurled, .—
Absol., for expedire se, to arm one's self for battle (only in Tac.), : multos secum expedire jubet,; 2, 99.
Trop., to bring out, extricate, release, free from any evil, obstacle, etc.: impeditum animum,; cf.: sapientis est, cum stultitiā suā impeditus sit, quoquo modo possit, se expedire,: haererem, nisi tu me expedisses,: ex servitute filium,; cf.: se ex turba,: se ab omni occupatione,: aliquem omni molestiā,; so, se aerumnis,: se crimine,: se cura,: civitatem malis obsidionalibus,: amor Lycisci me tenet, Unde expedire non queant amicorum consilia, : curae sagaces Expediunt (Claudiae manus) per acuta belli, bring or help through, ; cf.: per quot discrimina rerum Expedior?escape,: me multa impediverunt quae ne nunc quidem expedita sunt,: si vita nostra in aliquas insidias incidisset, omnis honesta ratio esset expediendae salutis,of obtaining safety,.—
Transf.
To put in order, arrange, set right: cum Antonio loquare velim, et rem, ut poteris, expedias,: expedire et conficere res,: rem frumentariam,; : negotia (with explicare),; cf. : nomina mea, per deos, expedi, exsolve,settle, pay,: nomen,: Faberianum,; cf. in a pun respecting a scholar unable to pay his debts: omnes solvere posse quaestiones, Unum difficile expedire nomen, Bibacul. ap. : quemadmodum expediam exitum hujus institutae orationis, non reperio,settle, arrange,; cf.: expediri quae restant vix poterunt. si hoc relinqueris,: consilia sua,: docte hanc fallaciam,put into operation,.—
Of speech, to disclose, unfold, explain, relate, narrate (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose; not in Cic., Cæs., or Quint.): qui tu misera's? mi expedi, (639 Ritschl): id ego aequum ac jus fecisse expedibo atque eloquar, will show, Enn. ap. ; Pac., Att.,: agedum, hoc mihi expedi,: altius omnem Expediam prima repetens ab origine famam,: pauca tibi e multis ... expediam dictis,: priusquam hujuscemodi rei initium expedio,: nunc originem, mores, et quo facinore dominationem raptum ierit, expediam,: me non tantum praevisa, sed subita expedire docuisti,: ea de caede quam verissime expediam,: promptius expediam quot, etc.,i. e. it will take me a shorter time to recount,.—
Reflex. of events, to develop, run their course, proceed: amoris arteis eloquar quem ad modum se expediant,; cf.: ut res vostrorum omnium bene expedire voltis,to make favorable progress, (Lorenz ad ; but Ussing reads me expedire, benefit me).—
Absol., res expedit, or impers., expedit (alicui—lit., it helps out, furthers, promotes; hence), it is serviceable, profitable, advantageous, useful, expedient (class.): nequiter paene expedivit prima parasitatio,: non igitur faciat, dixerit quis, quod utile sit, quod expediat? Immo intelligat, nihil nec expedire nec utile esse, quod sit injustum,; cf.: quid intersit sua, quid expediat,: ex utilitatis varietatibus, cum aliis aliud expediat, nasci discordias,; cf.: ut non idem expediret, incidere saepe,: quidquam Caesari ad diuturnitatem victoriae et dominationis,: non idem ipsis expedire et multitudini,—With an inf. clause as subject: expedit bonas esse vobis,; cf.: omnibus bonis expedit salvam esse rem publicam,: cui (reo) damnari expediret,: cum eam (pecuniam) in praediis collocari maxime expediret,: ubi vinci necesse est, expedit cedere,; et saep.—With subj. clause as subject after ut or ne (post-class.): expedire omnibus dicunt, ut singulae civitates suas leges habeant, Benecke ad loc.: expedit rei publicae, ne sua re quis male utatur,: neque expedire ut ambitione aliena trahatur,.—Absol.: tu si ita expedit, velim quamprimum conscendas,: sic magis expedit,: ut expediat causae,.—Hence, ex-pĕdītus, a, um, P. a., unimpeded, unincumbered, disengaged, free, easy, ready, at hand.
Of persons: cum ceteris quae habebat vadimonia differt, ut expeditus in Galliam proficisci posset,: inermos armati, impeditos expediti interficiunt, i. e. without baggage, Sisenn. ap. ; cf.: eo circiter hominum numero XVI. milia expedita cum omni equitatu Ariovistus misit,: legiones expeditae,; so of soldiers without baggage,; 6, 25, 1; 1, 27 fin. et saep.—As subst.: expĕdī-tus, i, m., a soldier lightly burdened, a swiftly marching soldier: latitudo (silvae) novem dierum iter expedito patet,: obviam fit ei Clodius expeditus in equo,; cf. Sagana,tucked up,: expedito nobis homine et parato opus est,ready, at hand, prompt,; cf.: expeditus ad caedem,: ad pronuntiandum,; cf.: facilis et expeditus ad dicendum,—
Of inanim. or abstr. things, convenient, at hand: iis expedito loco actuaria navigia relinquit,commodious,; cf.: via expeditior ad honores,: reditum in caelum patere optimo et justissimo cuique expeditissimum,: pecunia expeditissima quae erat, tibi decreta est,the readiest, the nearest at hand,; cf. rationes,: cena (with parca),: expeditissimum unguentorum,: probabili expedito, soluto, libero, nullā re implicato,: expedita erat et perfacile currens oratio,; cf.: expedita ac profluens dicendi celeritas,: inops ad ornandum, sed ad inveniendum expedita Hermagorae disciplina,: prope jam expeditam Caesaris victoriam interpellaverunt,achieved, —
In the neutr. absol.: in expedito esse, habere, etc., to be or have in readiness or at hand: quaedam sunt quidem in animo, sed parum prompta: quae incipiunt in expedito esse, quum dicta sunt,; cf.: promptum hoc et in expedito positum,: in expedito haberent integras copias ad opem ferendam,ready for action,.—Hence, adv.: ex-pĕdīte, without impediment, without difficulty, readily, promptly, quickly: in iis rebus celeriter expediteque percipiendis, quae, etc.,: expedite explicans quod proposuerat,: fabulatu's,: loqui,.—Comp.: non implicite et abscondite, sed patentius et expeditius,: navigare,: fit putatio,.—Sup.: ex quo te, quocumque opus erit, facillime et expeditissime conferas,.

la:verb:explico.gloss: to unfold, unfurl, uncoil, loosen, undo
senses: to unfold, unfurl, uncoil, loosen, undo
to spread out, stretch out, extend, display, deploy
to disentangle, solve, settle, arrange, regulate, adjust
la:verb:explico.html:
ex-plĭco, āvi and ŭi (the latter first in ; afterwards freq.; ; ; ; et saep.; cf. ), ātum or ĭtum (Cic. uses mostly atum, Caes. atum and itum; cf.
explicaturos,; with explicitis,; and, explicitius,; upon these forms v. Neue, Formenl. 2, pp. 479 sq., 550 sq.), 1, v. a., to unfold, uncoil, unroll, unfurl, spread out, loosen, undo (class.; esp. freq. in the trop. sense; syn.: expedio, extrico, enodo, enucleo; explano, expono, interpretor).
Lit.: velum,: non explicata veste neque proposito argento, etc.,spread out,: volumen,to open,: suas pennas (ales),: plenas plagas,: perturbatum et confusum agmen,to put in order,: capillum pectine, Müll.: fusos,to unwind,: frontem sollicitam,to free from wrinkles, to smooth,; for which: explicare seria contractae frontis,; cf. mare,i. e. to calm,: si ex his te laqueis exueris ac te aliqua via ac ratione explicaris,hast extricated, freed thyself,: se (ex funibus ancorarum),: inimicae et oves, difficile se (apibus) e lanis earum explicantibus,: se explicat angustum,.—
Transf., to spread out, stretch out, extend, deploy, display: aciem,; ; ; cf. ordinem,: agmen,: cohortes (longa legio),: se turmatim (equites),; cf. mid.: priusquam plane legiones explicari et consistere possent,; and: ut ordo omnium navium explicari posset,: per obstantis catervas Explicuit sua victor arma,: atria, congestos satis explicatura clientes,: ut forum laxaremus et usque ad atrium Libertatis explicaremus,extend,; cf.: unde pons in oppidum pertinens explicatur,: orbes (serpens),: frondes omnes (pampinus),: se (montes),: arida ligna in flammas (ignis),: convivium,i. e. to set out richly, to furnish,: explicavi meam rem post illa lucro,i. e. amplified, enlarged,.
Trop.
In gen. (very seldom): explica atque excute intelligentiam tuam, ut videas quae sit, etc.,display,: Siciliam multis undique cinctam periculis explicavit, has set at large, set free (qs. released from toils, snares), ; cf.: quemadmodum se explicent dicendo,: da operam, ut te explices, huc quam primum venias, Pompei. ap. , D. 2.—
In partic.
To disentangle, set in order, arrange, regulate, settle, adjust any thing complicated or difficult: pulcre ego hanc explicatam tibi rem dabo,, 20: peto a te, ut ejus negotia explices et expedias,: negotia,; cf. : belli rationem,; cf.: rationem salutis,: rem frumentariam,: si Faberius nobis nomen illud explicat, noli quaerere, quanti, settles, i. e. pays that item, : Faberianum, § 3; cf.: si qui debitores, quia non possint explicare pecuniam, differant solutionem,: consilium,; cf.: his explicitis rebus,: subvenire tempestati quavis ratione sapientis est; eoque magis, si plus adipiscare re explicatā boni, quam addubitatā mali,: ea, quae per defunctum inchoata sunt, per heredem explicari debent,: transii ad elegos: hos quoque feliciter explicui, (cf. under !*?): iter commode explicui, excepto quod, etc.,: fugam,: nihilo plus explicet ac si Insanire paret, etc.,will make no more out of it,.—
Of speech, to develop, unfold, set forth, exhibit, treat, state: vitam alterius totam explicare,: perfice, ut Crassus haec, quae coartavit et peranguste refersit in oratione sua, dilatet nobis atque explicet,: explicando excutiendoque verbo,: aliquid expedite,: aliquid apertissime planissimeque,: aliquid definitione,: funera fando,: philosophiam,; cf.: philosophiam diligentissime Graecis litteris,: summorum oratorum Graecas orationes,: geometricum quiddam aut physicum aut dialecticum (corresp. to expedire),: non de aegritudine solum, sed de omni animi perturbatione explicabo,: de scorpionibus et catapultis,: ut explicemus, quae sint materiae, etc.,.—Pass. impers.: quae vero auxilia sunt capitis, eo loco explicitum est,.—Hence,
explĭcātus, a, um, P. a.
Lit., spread out: Capua planissimo in loco explicata,: vallis,.—
Trop.
Well ordered, regular: in causa facili atque explicata,.—
Plain, clear: nisi explicata solutione non sum discessurus,.—Comp.: litterae tuae, quibus nihil potest esse explicatius, nihil perfectius,.— Sup.: explicatissima responsa,—
Assured, certain: nec habet explicatam aut exploratam rationem salutis suae,.—* Adv.: explĭ-cāte, plainly, clearly: qui distincte, qui explicate, qui abundanter et rebus et verbis dicunt,.—Comp.: explicatius,.—
explĭ-cĭtus, a, um, P. a. (acc. to II. B. 1.), lit., disentangled, i. e. free from obstacles, easy: in his erat angustiis res: sed ex propositis consiliis duobus explicitius videbatur, Ilerdam reverti,.!*? explĭcit, in late Lat., at the end of a book, is prob. an abbreviation of explicitus (est liber), the book is ended (acc. to signif. II. B. 1.); cf.: explicitum nobis usque ad sua cornua librum refers,: solemus completis opusculis ad distinctionem rei alterius sequentis medium interponere Explicit aut Feliciter aut aliquid istius modi, .

la:verb:experior.gloss: to attempt, to try; to test, to put to the test, to find out, to prove; therefore, to make trial of a person or thing
senses: to attempt, to try; to test, to put to the test, to find out, to prove; therefore, to make trial of a person or thing
to experience, to go through, to observe, to suffer, to endure, to sustain, to witness
la:verb:experior.html:
ex-pĕrĭor, pertus (
act. experiero, dub.), 4, v. dep. a. [ex- and root per-; Sanscr. par-, pi-parmi, conduct; Gr. περάω, pass through; πόρος, passage; πεῖρα, experience; Lat. porta, portus, peritus, periculum; Germ. fahren, erfahren; Eng. fare, ferry], to try a thing; viz., either by way of testing or of attempting it.
To try, prove, put to the test.
In tempp. praes. constr. with the acc., a rel. clause, or absol.
With acc.: habuisse aiunt domi (venenum), vimque ejus esse expertum in servo quodam ad eam rem ipsam parato,: taciturnitatem nostram,: amorem alicujus,, C, 1: his persuaserant, uti eandem belli fortunam experirentur,: judicium discipulorum,: in quo totas vires suas eloquentia experiretur,: imperium,: cervi cornua ad arbores subinde experientes, et saep.— With a personal object: vin' me experiri?make trial of me,: hanc experiamur, Ruhnk.: tum se denique errasse sentiunt, cum eos (amicos) gravis aliquis casus experiri cogit,: in periclitandis experiendisque pueris,.—So with se. reflex., to make trial of one's powers in any thing: se heroo (versu),

variis se studiorum generibus, : se in foro,.—

With a rel.-clause, ut, etc.: vosne velit an me regnare era quidve ferat Fors, Virtute experiamur, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 204, ed. Vahl.): lubet experiri, quo evasuru'st denique,: experiri libet, quantum audeatis,; cf. : in me ipso experior, ut exalbescam, etc.,; cf. with si: expertique simul, si tela artusque sequantur,.—
Absol.: experiendo magis quam discendo cognovi,: judicare difficile est sane nisi expertum: experiendum autem est in ipsa amicitia: ita praecurrit amicitia judicium tollitque experiendi potestatem,.—
In the tempp. perf., to have tried, tested, experienced, i. e. to find or know by experience: benignitatem tuam me experto praedicas,: omnia quae dico de Plancio, dico expertus in nobis,: experti scire debemus, etc.,: illud tibi expertus promitto,: dicam tibi, Catule, non tam doctus, quam, id quod est majus, expertus,: puellae jam virum expertae,; ; cf. : mala captivitatis,: id opera expertus sum esse ita,: expertus sum prodesse,: expertus, juvenem praelongos habuisse sermones,: ut frequenter experti sumus,.— Rarely in other tenses: et exorabile numen Fortasse experiar,may find,.—
To make trial of, in a hostile sense, to measure strength with, to contend with: ut interire quam Romanos non experiri mallet,: maritimis moribus mecum experitur,: ipsi duces cominus invicem experti,; ; cf.: hos cum Suevi, multis saepe bellis experti, finibus expellere non potuissent,: Turnum in armis,.
To undertake, to attempt, to make trial of, undergo, experience a thing.
In gen.: qui desperatione debilitati experiri id nolent, quod se assequi posse diffidant. Sed par est omnes omnia experiri, qui, etc.,; cf.: istuc primum experiar,: omnia experiri certum est, priusquam pereo,: omnia prius quam, etc.,: extrema omnia,; cf. also: sese omnia de pace expertum,: libertatem,i. e. to make use of, enjoy,: late fusum opus est et multiplex, etc. ... dicere experiar,: quod quoniam me saepius rogas, aggrediar, non tam perficiundi spe quam experiundi voluntate,.—With ut and subj.: nunc si vel periculose experiundum erit, experiar certe, ut hinc avolem,: experiri, ut sine armis propinquum ad officium reduceret,.—
In partic., jurid. t. t., to try or test by law, to go to law: aut intra parietes aut summo jure experietur,; cf.: in jus vocare est juris experiundi causa vocare,; : a me diem petivit: ego experiri non potui: latitavit,; : sua propria bona malaque, cum causae dicendae data facultas sit, tum se experturum,: postulare ut judicium populi Romani experiri (liceat),—Hence,
expĕrĭens, entis, P. a. (acc. to II.), experienced, enterprising, active, industrious (class.): homo gnavus et industrius, experientissimus ac diligentissimus arator,: promptus homo et experiens,, § 37: vir fortis et experiens,: vir acer et experiens,: comes experientis Ulixei,: ingenium,. —With gen.: genus experiens laborum,inured to, patient of,: rei militaris experientissimi duces,; cf. .—Comp. appears not to occur.—
expertus, a, um, P. a. (acc. to I.), in pass. signif., tried, proved, known by experience (freq. after the Aug. per.): vir acer et pro causa plebis expertae virtutis,: per omnia expertus,: indignitates homines expertos,: dulcedo libertatis,: industria,: artes,: saevitia, : confidens ostento sibi expertissimo,.—With gen.: expertos belli juvenes,; cf. .—Comp. and adv. appear not to occur.

la:verb:expono.gloss: to make conspicuous, to put something where everyone may see it: to expose, exhibit, display, set out
senses: to make conspicuous, to put something where everyone may see it: to expose, exhibit, display, set out
la:verb:expono.html:
ex-pōno, pŏsŭi, pŏsĭtum, 3 (ante-class.
perf. exposivit, ; sync. expostus,; ), v. a., to put or set out, to set forth, expose (class.; most freq. in the trop. signif.; cf.: expedio, explano, explico).
Lit.
In gen.: stravit pelliculis haedinis lectulos et exposuit vasa Samia,set out,: vasa,: apparatum in porticibus,; cf.: aliquid in publico,; cf. : herbam in sole,: aliquem ictu,to put out, turn out,: cubito,.—
In partic.
Of children, to expose: puellam ad necem,; ; ; ; ; cf. : ad januam matris,—
Naut. t. t.
To set on shore, to land, disembark: milites ex navibus,; for which: socios de puppibus,: milites in terram,: expositis omnibus copiis,; 1, 31 fin.; : ibi in terram,; ; cf.: in litora,: aegra mancipia in insulam,; but also with abl.: in Africa, Drak. N. cr.: in terra,: in litore,; ; ; ; : in portu,: ibi Themistoclem,: ad eum locum milites,: quibus regionibus exercitum exposuisset,fin.: expositum peregrinis arenis os,: quartā vix demum exponimur horā,: advexi frumentum; exposui, vendo meum, etc.,have unloaded, unpacked, opened,: merces,.—
To throw on the ground, throw down: paene exposivit cubito,.—
To throw overboard: si propter necessitatem adversae tempestatis expositum onus fuerit,.—
Mercant. t. t.: pecuniam, to offer a sum to one, place at one's disposal, to be ready to pay: de Oppio bene curasti, quod ei DCCC. exposuisti, (for which, aperuisti, ).—
Pregn., to leave exposed or unprotected, to expose, lay open (not ante-Aug.): ad ictus,; : ille ad omnes ictus expositus,: ne inermes provinciae barbaris nationibus exponerentur,: exercitum hosti,; : ceteris animalibus imbecillitatem hominum,; ; , ext. 2: piscibus beluisque,: exposito solibus loco,.—Pass. absol.: (iracundi) simplices videntur, quia expositi sunt, Sen. de Ira, 2, 16, 3.
Trop.
In gen.: totam causam, judices, explicemus atque ante oculos expositam consideremus,; cf.: vitam alterius in oculis conspectuque omnium exponere,: disciplina puerilis publice exposita,: orationem,to publish,; cf.: capita exposita nec explicata,: erant huic studio maxima exposita praemia,: praemium,to set forth, propose,: vitam suam exponere ad imitandum juventuti, id. Fragm. ap. : factum expositum ad imitandum,: exposita ad exemplum nostra re publica,: opprobrio ad omnium convicia exposito,: expositum ad invidiam nomen,: nomen Dei,to prostitute, dishonor,.—
In partic., of speech, to set forth, exhibit, relate, explain, expound; constr. with acc. and inf., or a rel. clause as object, or with de: coepit rationem hujus operis scientissime Gallus exponere,: talis coetus, qualem exposui,: quae adhuc exposui,: obscura dilucide,: rem pluribus verbis,: rem breviter,: mandata in senatu,: narrationem,: sententias ejus disputationis hoc libro,: artes rhetoricas,: disputationem alicui,: sermonem de amicitia alicui,: eadem multitudini,: expone igitur primum animos remanere post mortem, tum docebis, etc.,explain,: apud eosdem (censores), qui magistratu abierint, edant et exponant, quid in magistratu gesserint,: ex memoria alicui quid senatus censuerit,: ab initio, res quemadmodum gesta sit,; ; cf.: hoc de quo modo exposuit Antonius,; : expone nunc de reprehendendo,.—In abl. neutr. absol.: Caesar contione advocata ... exposito, quid iniquitas loci posset, etc., Oud.; so, exposito quod nuntiatum erat,: quasi gesta bello expositurus,: summum bonum exposuit vacuitatem doloris, i. q. definivit, be defined, Madv.; cf. ; and, expositio, ib. § 21.—Hence, expŏsĭtus, a, um, P. a., qs. publicly set out; hence, open, free, accessible.
Lit.: limen,: census,open to all,: numen (with nulli negatum),; cf.: (homo) obvius et expositus,.—As subst.: ex-pŏsĭta, ōrum, n., the open parts, those exposed to view: frontem ejus tantum novi et exposita, quae ostendit etiam transeuntibus,.—
Trop.
Accessible, affable: mores,.—
Of authors, intelligible, lucid: optimos quidem, sed tamen eorum candidissimum quemque et maxime expositum velim,.—
In a bad sense, common, vulgar: qui nihil expositum soleat deducere, etc.,.—Adv.: expŏ-sĭte, plainly, clearly: non exposite et aperte ostendere, sed reconditā significatione,.

la:verb:exprimo.html:
ex-prĭmo, pressi, pressum, 3, v. a.
premo
,
to press or squeeze out, to force out (class.).
Lit.: oleum ex malobathro,: sucum expresso semini,: sucum flore,: sucum radici,; cf.: vinum palmis, oleum sesamae (dat.), : oleum amygdalis,: sudorem de corpore,: lacrimulam oculos terendo,: si nubium conflictu ardor expressus se emiserit, id esse fulmen,: liquorem per densa foramina (cribri),; cf.: aquam in altum,: aquam in altitudinem,: quantum has (turres) quotidianus agger expresserat,had carried up, raised, Oud.: pecuniam alicui,; .—
Transf.
With an object denoting that out of which something is pressed or squeezed, to press, squeeze, wring: spongiam ex oleo vel aceto,: lanam ex vino vel aceto,; cf.: Venus madidas exprimit imbre comas,: spongiae expressae inter duas tabulas,: oleam,: folia rosae,: tuberculum,.—
To form by pressure, to represent, form, model, portray, express (mostly poet. and in postAug. prose; freq. in the elder Pliny): (faber) et ungues exprimet et molles imitabitur aere capillos,; cf.: alicujus furorem ... verecundiae ruborem,: expressa in cera ex anulo imago,: imaginem hominis gypso e facie ipsa,; cf.: effigiem de signis,: optime Herculem Delphis et Alexandrum, etc., et saep.: vestis stricta et singulos artus exprimens,exhibiting, showing,: pulcher aspectu sit athleta, cujus lacertos exercitatio expressit,has well developed, made muscular,.
Trop.
To squeeze or wring out, to extort, wrest, elicit: lex, quam ex natura ipsa arripuimus, hausimus, expressimus, qs. pressed out, : utilitas expressit nomina rerum,has imposed,: cf.: cum ab iis saepius quaereret, neque ullam omnino vocem exprimere posset,: expressa est Romanis necessitas obsides dandi,: confessionem concessi maris hosti,: confessionem cruciatu,: deditionem ultimā necessitate,: pecunia vi expressa et coacta,: tu si tuis blanditiis a Sicyoniis nummulorum aliquid expresseris,: risum magis quam gemitum, et saep.—With ut: expressi, ut conficere se tabulas negaret,have constrained,: expressit, ut polliceretur,. —
Transf. (acc. to I. B. 2.), to imitate, copy, represent, to portray, describe, express, esp. in words (cf. reddo): cum magnitudine animi tum liberalitate vitam patris et consuetudinem expresserit,i. e. imitated,: lex expressa ad naturam,: vitia imitatione ex aliquo expressa,: rem ante oculos ponit, cum exprimit omnia perspicue, ut res prope dicam manu tentari possit,; cf. § 63: hanc speciem Pasiteles caelavit argento et noster expressit Archias versibus,: mores alicujus oratione,: multas nobis imagines fortissimorum virorum expressas scriptores Graeci et Latini reliquerunt,; cf. : in Platonis libris omnibus fere Socrates exprimitur,: Mithridaticum bellum magnum atque difficile totum ab hoc expressum est, depicted to the life, ; cf.: ut Euryalum exprimat infans,may resemble,.—With rel.-clause as object: diligenter, quae vis subjecta sit vocibus,: exprimere non possum, quanto sim gaudio affectus,tell, express,; : verbis exprimere quid quis sentiat,: quod exprimere dicendo sensa possumus,: mores in scriptis exprimere,.—Of translating into another language, to render, translate: si modo id exprimere Latine potuero,; cf. : κατάληψιν, verbum e verbo exprimentes comprehensionem dicemus, : nec tamen exprimi verbum e verbo necesse erit,; cf.: verbum de verbo expressum extulit,: fabellae Latinae ad verbum de Graecis expressae,; .—Of words, to pronounce, utter: nolo exprimi litteras putidius nolo obscurari neglegentius,with affected distinctness,: verba,; ; —Rarely of a personal object: oratorem imitando effingere atque exprimere,: moderatorem rei publicae nostris libris diligenter expressimus,.—Hence, expressus, a, um, P. a., clearly exhibited, prominent, distinct, visible, manifest, clear, plain, express (syn. solidus, opp. adumbratus).
Lit.: species deorum, quae nihil concreti habeat, nihil solidi, nihil expressi, nihil eminentis,; cf.: litterae lituraeque omnes assimulatae, expressae,: corpora lacertis expressa,powerful, muscular,:protinus omnibus membris, expressus infans,fully formed,.—
Trop.
In gen.: habuit Catilina permulta maximarum non expressa signa, sed adumbrata virtutum,; cf.: est gloria solida quaedam res et expressa, non adumbrata, (v. Madv. ad ): indicia solida et expressa,; cf.: veri juris germanaeque justitiae solida et expressa effigies,: expressa sceleris vestigia,: expressiora et illustriora,; cf. ; and: quid expressius atque signatius in hanc causam?.—
Expressa carmina Battiadae, translated, .—Of distinct pronunciation: vitia oris emendet, ut expressa sint verba, ut suis quaeque litterae sonis enuntientur,: expressior sermo,: expressior loquacitas generi picarum est,. —In a bad sense, of a too emphatic, affected pronunciation: sonus erat dulcis: litterae neque expressae neque oppressae, ne aut obscurum esset aut putidum, Cic Off. 1, 37, 133.—Hence, adv.: expressē. *
Lit., with pressure, strongly: artus expressius fricare,.—
Trop., expressly, distinctly, clearly: conscripta exempla,: quod ipsum expressius Hesiodus hoc versu significavit,.—Of pronunciation, distinctly: ut ea (R littera) a nullo expressius efferretur,ext.

la:verb:exploro.gloss: to investigate, search out, seek, discover, examine, explore
senses: to investigate, search out, seek, discover, examine, explore
to test, try, put to the proof
la:verb:exploro.html:
ex-plōro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to search out, seek to discover, to examine, investigate, explore (class.; in Cic. esp. freq. in the part. perf. and P. a.; syn.: speculor, scitor, sciscitor, percontor, quaero, interrogo).
In gen.
With acc.: explora rem totam,: fugam domini,: ambitum Africae,: altera (manus) motu caecum iter explorat,: vehiculorum onera,: glebas gustu,: panis potionisque bonitatem gustu, et saep.: ad explorandum idoneum locum castris,for choosing out,: insidias,to seek out,.—
With rel. clause: explorare, qui homines inhabitarent,: apud se explorare, an expediat sibi consilium,: exploratum est, ubi controversia incipiat,.—
In the part. perf., examined, ascertained, known: exploratum et provisum,: jam explorata nobis sunt ea, quae, etc.,: perspecta et explorata perscribere,; cf.: res non incertis jactatae rumoribus, sed compertae et exploratae,: de numero eorum omnia se habere explorata Remi dicebant,; .—In abl. neutr. absol.: explorato, it being ascertained, i. e. when he knew: explorato, jam profectos amicos,.
In partic.
In milit. lang., to spy out, reconnoitre: speculatoribus in omnes partes dimissis, explorat, quo commodissime itinere vallum transire possit,; cf. : itinera egressusque ejus, postremo loca atque tempora cuncta explorat,: Siciliam adiit, Africam exploravit,: occulte explorare loca,: explorato hostium consilio,.—In the neutr. absol.: ante explorato et subsidiis positis,; so ; fin.—
To try, test, put to the proof (perh. not ante-Aug.): et suspensa focis explorat robora fumus,: taurus in adversis explorat cornua truncis,; cf.: hoc jugulo dextram explora,: animos,; : explorans quid hostes agerent,: haec exploranda per impigros juvenes esse,: secundae res animos,: tyranni fidem,.—Hence, explōrātus, a, um, P. a.Lit., ascertained; hence, established, confirmed, certain, sure: ut ei jam exploratus et domi conditus consulatus videretur,: magna et prope explorata

spes, ; ; : victoria,: ratio,: litterae exploratae a timore,i. e. affording certainty, confidence, et saep.: de quo mihi exploratum est, ita esse, ut scribis,I am certain, convinced,; cf. : quis est tam stultus, cui sit exploratum, se ad vesperum esse victurum?: in qua (amicitia) nihil fidum, nihil exploratum habeas,: exploratam habere pacem,: (Deus) habet exploratum, fore, etc.,: pro explorato habebat, etc.,.—Comp.: facilior et exploratior devitatio legionum fore videtur, etc.,.—Sup.: exploratissima victoria,.—Adv.: explōrātē, with certainty, for a certainty, securely, surely (for the most part only in Cic.): haec ita sentio, judico, ad te explorate scribo,, b. 3; cf. judicare, Planc. in : satis explorate perceptum et cognitum,: navigare,.—Comp.: exploratius promittere,.— Sup. seems not to occur.

la:verb:explano.html:
ex-plāno, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. *
Lit., to flatten or spread out: suberi cortex in denos pedes undique explanatus,.—
Trop., of speech, to make plain or clear, to explain (class.: syn.: explico, expono, interpretor): qualis differentia sit honesti et decori, facilius intelligi quam explanari potest,; cf. : rem latentem explicare definiendo, obscuram explanare interpretando, etc.,: explanare apertiusque dicere aliquid,: docere et explanare,: aliquid conjecturā,: rem,: quem amicum tuum ais fuisse istum, explana mihi,: de cujus hominis moribus pauca prius explananda sunt, quam initium narrandi faciam,.—Pass. impers.: juxta quod flumen, aut ubi fuerit, non satis explanatur,.—
To utter distinctly: et ille juravit, expressit, explanavitque verba, quibus, etc.,.—Hence, explānātus, a, um, P. a. (acc. to II.), plain, distinct (rare): claritas in voce, in lingua etiam explanata vocum impressio,i. e. an articulate pronunciation,: parum explanatis vocibus sermo praeruptus, Sen. de Ira, 1, 1, 4.—Adv.ex-plānāte, plainly, clearly, distinctly: scriptum,.—Comp.: ut definire rem cum explanatius, tum etiam uberius (opp. presse et anguste),.

Transf., in gen., destitute or devoid of, free from, without (freq. and class.).— Constr. in class. lang. with gen.; ante-class. and in Sall. also with abl.
With gen.: omnium vitiūm expers, Titin. ap. : laboris,: omnis eruditionis expers atque ignarus,: veritatis,: negotii publici,: humanitatis,: nuptiarum,: viri,: ferae rationis et orationis expertes,: Chium (vinum) maris expers,without sea-water,: sui,; cf.: ut nulla ejus vitae pars summae turpitudinis esset expers,: vis consili expers, et saep.: expers matris imperii, free from, i. e. neglectful of, disobedient to, .—

la:verb:expendo.html:
ex-pendo, di, sum, 3, v. a.,
to weigh out, weigh.
Lit.
In gen. (very rare): aliquem,: ut jam expendantur, non numerentur pecuniae,: bacam, nucem,.—With abl. of that against which any thing is weighed: hunc hominem decet auro expendi,i. e. is worth his weight in gold,.—Poet.: ibat et expenso planta morata gradu,measured, (16).—
In partic., to weigh out money in payment, to pay out, pay; to lay out, expend (class.; syn.: pendo, impendo, pondero, solvo, luo): ante pedes praetoris in foro expensum est auri pondo centum,: nummos nominibus certis,: usuras gravissimas,: viginti milia talenta in hos sumptus,.—With abl.: aurum auro expendetur, argentum argento exaequabitur,. —
In the part. perf. as a neutr. subst.: expensum, i, money paid, a payment: bene igitur ratio accepti atque expensi inter nos convenit,of debt and credit,; : in codicem expensum et receptum referre,: probari debere pecuniam datam consuetis modis, expensi latione, mensae rationibus, chirographi exhibitione, etc.,.—Esp. freq.: ferre alicui expensum or pecuniam expensam, to set down, enter, charge, reckon, account a sum as paid (opp. accipio): quod minus Dolabella Verri acceptum retulit quam Verres illi expensum tulerit ... quid proderat tibi te expensum illis non tulisse?, §§ 100 and 102: haec pecunia necesse est aut data aut expensa lata aut stipulata sit,: pecunias ferre (opp. acceptas referre), Auct. B. Alex. 56, 3: homines prope quadringentos produxisse dicitur, quibus sine fenore pecunias expensas tulisset, had set down, i. e. lent, .—Rarely transf., of other things: legio, quam expensam tulit C. Caesari Pompeius, i. e. transferred, Cael. ap. ; for which also: expenso ferre vestem supellectilis nomine, .
Trop.
(Acc. to I. A.) To weigh mentally, to ponder, estimate, consider, judge, decide (class.): equidem cum colligo argumenta causarum, non tam ea numerare soleo quam expendere,; cf.: in dissensione civili ... expendendos cives non numerandos puto,: omnia expendet ac seliget,: vos in privatis minimarum rerum judiciis testem diligenter expenditis,: singula animo suo,: haec arte aliqua,; cf.: verba arte,: omnes casus,: belli consilia,: causam meritis,to decide, et saep.: quae contemplantes expendere oportebit, quid quisque habeat sui,: Hannibalem,: quid conveniat nobis,.—
(Acc. to I. B. 1.) To pay a penalty, suffer a punishment (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): poenas Jovi expendisse (shortly after, in prose, poenas pendens), Att. ap. ; cf.: infanda per orbem Supplicia et scelerum poenas expendimus omnes,: dignas poenas pro talibus ausis,: poenas capite,: dura supplicia,.—Hence, to pay for, expiate: scelus,: dignum pretium Poeno,.—
(Cf. I. B. 2.) Ipsam facilitati suae expensum ferre debere, i. e. have to ascribe to, : creditores suae negligentiae expensum ferre debeant,.—* expense, adv., largely, very much (late Lat.), Theod. Prisc. de Diaeta, 13.

ex-plĕo, ēvi, ētum, 2 (archaic form explenunt, for explent, acc. to ; cf.: solinunt, nequinunt, danunt, for solent, nequeunt, dant; v. do, redeo and soleo

In partic.
To satisfy, sate, glut, appease a longing, or one who longs (the fig. being that of filling or stuffing with food): quas (litteras Graecas) sic avide arripui quasi diuturnam sitim explere cupiens,: famem,; cf.: jejunam cupidinem,: libidines (with satiare), ap. (Rep. 6, 1); cf.: explere cupiditates, satiare odium,: libidinem,: odium factis dictisque,; : desiderium,: iram,; cf.: omnem exspectationem diuturni desiderii nostri,: avaritiam pecuniā,; : spem omnium,; ; et saep.: me,; cf.: non enim vereor, ne non scribendo te expleam,: se caede diu optata,: tantum regem (divitiis),: aliquem muneribus,; ; : omnis suos divitiis,: animum suum (amore),: animum gaudio,; cf. ; : corda tuendo,; cf.: expleri mentem nequit ardescitque tuendo Phoenissa,: expletur lacrimis dolor,: alicujus crudelitatem sanguine, Crassus ap. .— And reflex.: ut eorum agris expleti atque saturati cum hoc cumulo quaestus decederent,—Poet.: aliquem alicujus rei (cf. To fulfil, discharge, execute, perform a duty: amicitiae munus,: susceptum rei publicae munus,: excusatione officium scribendi,: mandatum,.—
Of time, to complete, finish, bring to a close: tum signis omnibus ad idem principium stellisque revocatis, expletum annum habeto,: fatales annos,: quosdam in Aetolia ducentos annos explere,: explebat annum trigesimum,.*
(Ex in privative signif.; v. ex, III. A.). To unload: navibus explebant sese terrasque replebant, i. e. disembarked, exonerabant se, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 310 ed. Vahl.).—Hence, ex-plētus, a, um, P. a., full, complete, perfect: quod undique perfectum expletumque sit omnibus suis numeris ac partibus,: undique expleta et perfecta forma honestatis,: ea, quae natura desiderat, expleta cumulataque habere,: expletum omnibus suis partibus,: vita animi corporisque expleta virtutibus,: expleta rerum comprehensio,.—Absol.: parum expleta desiderant,.
